content:
The FDA first approved Enhertu (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) for breast cancer on **December 20, 2019**. This was an **accelerated approval** for adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who had received two or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens in the metastatic setting.

Since that initial approval, the FDA has expanded Enhertu's breast cancer indications several times:

- **May 4, 2022** — Converted to regular (full) approval for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after just one prior anti-HER2 therapy, based on the DESTINY-Breast03 trial.
- **August 5, 2022** — Approved for HER2-low metastatic breast cancer.
- **January 27, 2025** — Expanded to include HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer.
- **December 15, 2025** — Approved in combination with pertuzumab for first-line treatment of HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.
- **May 15, 2026** — Approved for two new indications in HER2-positive early breast cancer.
